correctness.rationale: Direct substitution into the two orbit equations yields b=x^(p+1)(r-a)=x^(p+1)r^p(1-a r) and hence the necessary-and-sufficient ratio equation. Put r=e^(2t); R_p(t)=sinh((p-1)t)/sinh((p+1)t) is positive and strictly decreasing because u*coth(u) is strictly increasing (derivative numerator sinh(u)cosh(u)-u has derivative 2 sinh(u)^2>0). The endpoint limits are (p-1)/(p+1) and 0, proving exact existence and uniqueness for all real p>1. At p=2, symmetric sums P=aS^2/(1+a), b=a^2 S^3/(1+a) and discriminant yield the stated positive coordinates. The two-step multiplier is 9a^2+6a-2, crossing -1 at (sqrt(2)-1)/3, increasing to 1 as a->1/3. Hyperbolic attraction and repulsion follow from the standard one-dimensional derivative test. Boundary multipliers are correctly called neutral only; no nonlinear critical/global claim.

value.rationale: The map is the exact one-dimensional negative-knowledge-elasticity reduction studied in the 2026 innovation-cycle source. The source has an existence/stability distinction; the result determines the full number and positions of positive primitive two-cycles for all real powers p>1, and gives an independent exact attracting-versus-repelling boundary for the natural inverse-square exponent. Parameter b changes scale but not stability. This is a motivated natural complete period-two classification, not an arbitrary finite tabulation, although the proof is elementary and does not classify other periods or global dynamics.
